steps.title: Import Component and FormsModule
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and FormsModule from '@angular/forms'
steps.hint: Use two separate import statements - one for Component and one for FormsModule from their respective packages
steps.seedCode: // Import the necessary Angular modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: Component and FormsModule are imported and available for use in creating an Angular component with form handling capabilities
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and FormsModule is imported from '@angular/forms'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've imported both Component and FormsModule which are essential for creating Angular components with form handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have both imports - Component from '@angular/core' and FormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' and FormsModule from '@angular/forms'. These are needed for component creation and form handling.

steps.title: Create the ControlledInput component
steps.instruction: Create a component class named ControlledInputComponent with the @Component decorator.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with a selector and template property, then create the class with 'export class ControlledInputComponent'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic Angular component class with the @Component decorator is defined.
successCriteria: ControlledInputComponent class is created with @Component decorator including selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the basic structure for your Angular component with the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component has both the @Component decorator and the class declaration.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to use the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, followed by the export class declaration.

steps.title: Initialize input value property
steps.instruction: Add an inputValue property to the ControlledInputComponent class and initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the public access modifier and initialize the property directly in the class body with an empty string value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have an inputValue property initialized as an empty string to hold the controlled input state.
successCriteria: The ControlledInputComponent class contains an inputValue property initialized with an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the inputValue property that will store the current state of the controlled input.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the inputValue property is initialized with an empty string ('').
steps.feedbackWrong: The inputValue property needs to be added to the class and initialized with an empty string. Check the class body inside the ControlledInputComponent.

steps.title: Define input change handler method
steps.instruction: Add an onInputChange method inside the ControlledInputComponent class that takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue property with the input's value
steps.hint: Create a method that accepts an event parameter and sets this.inputValue to event.target.value
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an onInputChange method that can handle input events and update the inputValue property
successCriteria: An onInputChange method is defined that takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the input change handler method that will update the component's state when the input value changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue property with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onInputChange method should accept an event parameter and use event.target.value to update this.inputValue.

steps.title: Add component template with basic structure
steps.instruction: Replace the placeholder comment in the template with a heading that says 'Controlled Input Demo'
steps.hint: Add an h2 element with the text 'Controlled Input Demo' inside the existing div container
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding a heading to a template template: `

My App Title

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a heading that displays 'Controlled Input Demo'
successCriteria: An h2 element with the text 'Controlled Input Demo' is added to the template
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the heading to structure your controlled input component template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use an h2 element with the exact text 'Controlled Input Demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add an h2 element inside the div with the text 'Controlled Input Demo'.

steps.title: Add the controlled input element
steps.instruction: Add an input element with ngModel directive bound to inputValue and wire the input event to onInputChange method.
steps.hint: Use [(ngModel)] for two-way data binding and (input) event binding to connect the input field to your component properties and methods.
steps.expectedOutcome: An input element with two-way data binding that updates the inputValue property and calls the onInputChange method when the user types.
successCriteria: Input element is added with [(ngModel)] bound to inputValue and (input) event bound to onInputChange method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created a controlled input with two-way data binding using ngModel and event handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your input has both [(ngModel)]="inputValue" for two-way binding and (input)="onInputChange($event)" for the event handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input needs both ngModel for two-way data binding and an input event handler. Check the syntax for Angular's two-way binding.

steps.title: Display the current input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the template that displays the current inputValue using Angular string interpolation
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display the inputValue property in the paragraph
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a property in the template

Welcome {{ userName }}!
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element is added to the template that displays the current value of inputValue using string interpolation
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element that uses {{ inputValue }} to display the current input value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added string interpolation to display the current input value. Now you can see the controlled input's value being displayed in real-time.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using the correct Angular string interpolation syntax with double curly braces {{ }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add a paragraph element inside the template and use {{ inputValue }} to display the current value of the input.

steps.title: Add a clear button
steps.instruction: Add a button element with text 'Clear' that has a click handler calling a method to clear the inputValue.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to call a method that will reset the inputValue property to an empty string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clear button is added to the template that will reset the input value when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element with 'Clear' text and click handler is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added a clear button that will allow users to reset the input value.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has both the 'Clear' text and a click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clear button needs to have 'Clear' as the text and use (click) event binding to call a handler method.

steps.title: Add character count display
steps.instruction: Add a span element below the paragraph that displays the character count of the current inputValue
steps.hint: Use string interpolation to show the length property of inputValue inside a span element
steps.expectedOutcome: A span element is added that shows the character count of the input value, updating dynamically as the user types
successCriteria: A span element is present that displays the character count using inputValue.length
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! The character count display shows how controlled inputs enable reactive UI updates based on state changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the span shows the character count using the length property of inputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a span element that uses string interpolation to display inputValue.length as the character count.

steps.title: Configure FormsModule in component imports
steps.instruction: The FormsModule is already imported at the top of the file and added to the component's imports array. Verify that FormsModule is properly configured to enable template-driven forms functionality in your ControlledInputComponent.
steps.hint: Check that FormsModule appears in both the import statement at the top and in the component's imports array to enable Angular's form directives.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ControlledInputComponent is properly configured with FormsModule to enable template-driven forms functionality.
successCriteria: FormsModule is imported from '@angular/forms' and included in the component's imports array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Your ControlledInputComponent is now properly configured with FormsModule, enabling full template-driven forms functionality including two-way data binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure FormsModule is both imported at the top and included in the component's imports array.
steps.feedbackWrong: FormsModule needs to be imported from '@angular/forms' and added to the component's imports array to enable form directives.
